## Why v2 (what was broken in v1)

1. **"This chat" was usually empty.** Attribution rescanned a chat's transcripts on
every index requ

est, keyed on the global file list (any new file anywhere forced
a 10-100 s rescan; the client waite

d 2 s), and it ignored tool/ptc-dispatch-start
rows whose arguments are objects, that is every write

made from inside run_code.
v2 tails each zstd transcript frame by frame from a stored cursor (full

backfill
of 892 MB: 75 s once; steady state: milliseconds) and also records explicit
claims from the

CLI ($DSH_SESSION_ID). Index requests are ~30 ms with ETag/304.
2. **The .md opened instead of the

page.** .md requested by a browser now renders
(?raw=1 or curl gets the source), md+html pairs are o

ne artifact, /report/x.html
is rendered on the fly from x.md, and chat links to ~/reports/* open the

rendered artifact in the tab.
3. **Kit pages did not adapt to text length.** Long words, KPI values

, table cells,
headings and TOC entries now wrap; widths adapt to the content (wide tables get a
wid

e page); chart label space is measured, long x labels rotate, labels with
commas parse, ticks are ro

rt label space is measured, long x labels rotate, labels with
commas parse, ticks are round numbers.
## Token economics

- Templates before everything: a known kind of deliverable is a JSON data file (a few
KB) filled int

o a finished layout, instead of a page written from scratch.
- Markdown first (35-40 % fewer output

tokens than hand-written HTML on a typical
report, far more with charts), rendered server-side: no r

ender step, no HTML in
context.
- Edit, never rewrite: every save is snapshotted and live-reloads th

e preview.
- state-set pushes data into a running app without touching its code.
- Pick-and-ask send

s a compact reference (selector + heading + text) instead of
the user pasting or the agent re-readin

g the page.
- Libraries are served locally, never inlined; the CLI + skill cost zero tokens
per turn
until used (no tool schemas in every request).
## Templates
A template is a finished, tested layout for one kind of deliverable. An agent writes only the data (

JSON); it
is validated against the template's JSON Schema, local images and videos are copied next t

o the artifact, and the
page is written into the artifacts folder (`ARTIFACT_DIR`, default `~/report

s`). Bundled: `report-text`, `article`,
`dashboard`, `review-queue`, `video-explainer`, `video-page`
(see templates/README.md).
### For users
- Nothing to set up: after installing the plugin and restarting `dsh web`, every agent on the instal

l sees the
four tools below and the `publish-artifact` skill, whose first step is "templates first".

- Your own templates: agents save them with `artifact_template_save` into the user library
`${DSH_H

OME:-~/.dsh}/artifacts/templates`. You can also drop template folders there by hand, or point
`ARTIF

ACT_TEMPLATES` (colon separated) at your own libraries.
- Search order, first match per id wins: `$A

RTIFACT_TEMPLATES`, `~/estate/templates/artifacts` (if it exists),
